paragraph: Angola's statistics law is [Lei n.º 3/11 of 14 January 2011](<https://lex.ao/docs/assembleia-nacional/2011/lei-n-o-3-11-de-14-de-janeiro/>), which replaced the statistics law of 1996. In the last twelve months, [Presidential Decree 43/26 of 10 March 2026](<https://lex.ao/docs/presidente-da-republica/2026/decreto-presidencial-n-o-43-26-de-10-de-marco/>) made the statistics institute the central executive body of the national statistical system under the law. It revoked its statute of 2017. The institute [opened a public consultation on a proposed revision on 29 September 2026](<https://angop.ao/noticias/economia/ine-inicia-recolha-de-contribuicoes-para-nova-lei-estatistica/>). No source found shows the statistics council meeting or a penalty under the law.

Burundi's statistics law is [Loi n°1/08 of 20 May 2021](<https://amategeko.gov.bi/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/BOB_No5BIS-2021.pdf>), which recast the law of 25 September 2007. [Loi n°1/18 of 24 July 2023 amended it](<https://www.insbu.bi/documents/lois/Loi-N%C2%B0-1-18-du-24-juillet-2023-portant-organisation-du-SSN-du-Burundi.pdf>) and makes every nationally representative survey subject to a statistical visa. In the last twelve months, [the national statistical information committee held its 13th session on 6 November 2026, chaired by the Prime Minister](<https://burundi-news.com/articles/fr/renforcement-du-systeme-statistique-national-au-burundi.html>). It discussed draft decrees on an enterprise classification and an order of statistics professionals. No source found shows a penalty under the law.

Benin's statistics law is [Loi n° 2022-07 of 27 June 2022](<https://instad.bj/images/docs/lois_decrets/LOI%20N%C2%B0%202022-07%20DU%2027%20JUIN%202022%20STATISTIQUE.pdf>), adopted by the National Assembly on 2 June 2022. The statistics strategy of 2020 said activity then rested on [a law of 12 April 2000 creating the National Statistics Council](<https://instad.bj/images/docs/cns/programme-SNDS/SNDS-3%20VF.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [Decree 2026-002 of 21 January 2026](<https://sgg.gouv.bj/doc/decret-2026-002/download>) cited the 2022 law among its legal bases; it was cited and not changed. No source found names a decree, regulation or order made under the law. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Burkina Faso's statistics law is [Loi n°036-2021/AN of 6 December 2021](<https://www.insd.bf/sites/default/files/2022-05/loi_036_statistiques.pdf>), which repealed the law of 2007. [Decree 2025-1095 of 26 August 2025 was adopted in application of it](<https://www.insd.bf/sites/default/files/2026-04/Plan%20strat%C3%A9gique_2026-2030%20de%20l%27INSD_0.pdf>) and [sets up the national statistics council](<https://www.insd.bf/Coordination-statistiques/cns>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The [statistics master plan of December 2025](<https://www.insd.bf/sites/default/files/2026-04/%5BSDS5-BF%5D_SDS-2026-2030.pdf>) says three application decrees are available. It says the texts on the statistics development fund were still awaited.

Botswana's statistics law is the [Statistics Act, No. 15 of 2009](<https://statsbots.org.bw/sites/default/files/documents/Statistics%20Act%202009.pdf>), which establishes Statistics Botswana and commenced on 1 December 2010. Its [annual report for 2023/24 says the Board was constituted in conformity with section 6 of the Act](<https://statsbots.org.bw/sites/default/files/documents/Statistics%20Botswana%20Annual%20Report%202023-24.pdf>) in the year to 31 March 2024, with nine members appointed by the Minister. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

The Central African Republic's statistics law is [Law No. 01.008 of 16 July 2001](<https://unstats.un.org/unsd/dnss/docViewer.aspx?docID=2170>), which creates the national statistical system, the national statistics council and the statistics institute. In the last twelve months, [a workshop in Bangui on 23 April 2026 validated a draft law to replace it](<https://www.icasees.org/index.php/actualites/332-icasees-atelier-pour-la-validation-du-projet-de-loi-statistique-en-republique-centrafricaine>). The 2001 law stays in force until the draft is adopted. No decree, regulation or order made under the 2001 law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Côte d'Ivoire's statistics law is law 2013-537 of 30 July 2013, amended by law 2020-950 of 7 December 2020. On 18 June 2025 [the Council of Ministers adopted three decrees applying the statistics law](<https://web.sgg.gouv.ci/publications/conseils-des-ministres/details/3009>). They set how the survey and census visa is granted, the conditions and prices for statistical products, and how administrative files pass to the system for statistical use. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows the statistics council meeting or a visa granted under the decrees.

Cameroon's statistics law is [law n°2020/010 of 20 July 2020](<https://www.prc.cm/fr/multimedia/documents/8414-loi-n-2020-010-du-20-07-2020-activite-statistique-cm>). [Decree n°2021/690 of 2 December 2021](<https://www.afristat.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/CM02_Decret-application-loi-statistique.pdf>) sets the rules for applying it, and is the one rule found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need the law applied in the past three years: its council or board appointed or meeting, a standard, release calendar or survey approval issued under it, a rule made under it, or a penalty.

The Democratic Republic of the Congo made its first statistics law in 2026, after a bill [drafted in December 2024 by the National Institute of Statistics](<https://drc.unfpa.org/fr/news/rdc-masina-commune-pilote-pour-la-digitalisation-des-faits-de-letat-civil>). In the last twelve months, [the Council of Ministers adopted a draft ordonnance-loi on 28 August 2026](<https://beto.cd/ordonnance-loi-statistique-rdc-recensement-habilitation/>). The state news agency reported on 12 September 2026 that [the President had signed it](<https://acp.cd/nation/le-president-tshisekedi-fixe-les-conditions-dorganisation-de-lactivite-statistique-en-rdc/>). [On 21 October 2026 the Senate ratified it as ordonnance-loi n° 26/015 of 7 September 2026](<https://actualite.cd/2026/10/22/rdc-le-senat-ratifie-lunanimite-lordonnance-loi-portant-organisation-de-lactivite>). No decree, regulation or order made under it has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Congo's statistics law is law no. 36-2018 on official statistics, whose text is in [the Journal officiel, issue no. 42 of 18 October 2018](<https://www.sgg.cg/JO/2018/congo-jo-2018-42.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [INS Congo issued its advance release calendar for 2026 in October 2026, stating that it answers the requirements of law 36-2018](<https://www.ins-congo.cg/uploads/publications/ins_6ad8553134ba03.75061568.pdf>). The calendar sets the dates on which the year's official statistics are to be released. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

The Comoros' statistics law is [Loi n°11-003/AU of 26 March 2011](<https://justice.gouv.km/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/loi-n-11-003au-du-26-mars-2011-portant-organisation-et-reglementation-des-activites-statistiques-aux-comores.pdf>), adopted by the Assembly of the Union. A later decree records in its preamble that [the law was promulgated by decree N°11-142/PR of 14 July 2011](<https://pfss-comores.org/ressources/download/19>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Cabo Verde's statistics law is [Lei n.º 48/IX/2019, published in the Boletim Oficial of 19 February 2019](<https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/View/40755>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: [the board of the statistics institute said on 1 June 2026 that it asserts its technical independence under the law](<https://expressodasilhas.cv/pais/2026/06/01/ine-rejeita-acusacoes-de-manipulacao-de-dados-e-reafirma-independencia-tecnica/>). In 2024 [a cooperation mission of Statistics Portugal supported the revision of the law](<https://www.ine.pt/ine_novidades/Coopstat_n25/13/>). No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Djibouti's [Loi n° 26/AN/18/8ème L of 27 February 2019](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/loi-n26-an-18-8eme-l-relatif-a-la-creation-de-linstitut-national-de-la-statistique-de-djibouti-insd/>) created the national statistics institute. [A law of 18 February 2021 renamed it INSTAD](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/loi-n108-an-20-8eme-l-portant-modification-de-la-loi-n26-an-18-8eme-l-relative-a-la-creation-de-linstitut-national-de-la-statistique-de-djibouti-insd/>). [Decree 2023-185 named the eleven members of its board for three-year terms from 6 July 2023](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/decret-n2023-185-pr-mefi-portant-nomination-des-membres-du-conseil-dadministration-de-linstitut-de-la-statistique-de-djibouti-instad/>). No change to the law has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows the board or council meeting under the law since 2023, or a standard, survey approval or penalty. Mature would need the law applied in the past three years: its council or board appointed or meeting, a standard, release calendar or survey approval issued under it, a rule made under it, or a penalty.

Algeria's statistics office said in [a presentation of 1 July 2025](<https://unstats.un.org/unsd/methodology/dataquality/meetings/training-wks-Jul2025/Session2_ALGERIA.pdf>) that Legislative Decree 94-01 of 15 January 1994 remains the legal basis of official statistics. It said the law is under review. [Executive Decree 95-159 of 3 June 1995](<https://unstats.un.org/unsd/dnss/docViewer.aspx?docID=2193>) restates the statutes of the office and is the one rule found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need the law applied in the past three years: its council or board appointed or meeting, a standard, release calendar or survey approval issued under it, a rule made under it, or a penalty.

Egypt's statistics law is [Law No. 35 of 1960 on statistics and censuses](<https://old.capmas.gov.eg/Pages/StaticPages.aspx?page_id=23>), issued on 9 February 1960 and amended by Law No. 28 of 1982. The statistics agency publishes it as the law that regulates statistical work. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found, and no bill to replace it. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

A review of the statistics office's cooperation with Statistics Norway, [published on 8 January 2007](<https://www.norad.no/contentassets/7f7da719f25e49169fd844b5bb9b6f15/mid-term-review-of-cooperation-between-national-statistics-office-in-eritrea-and-statistics-norway.pdf>), says the Statistical Proclamation had been submitted to government. Its formal issue was still pending. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a statistics law is in force, or that the proclamation was issued or withdrawn after 2007. Establishing would need a statistics law in force: an act, ordinance or decree with the force of law that governs official statistics or sets up the national statistics office.

Ethiopia's statistics law is the [Central Statistics Authority Establishment Proclamation No. 442/2005](<https://www.lawethiopia.com/images/federal_proclamation/proclamations_by_number/442.pdf>), published in the Federal Negarit Gazeta on 20 April 2005. In the last twelve months, [the House of People's Representatives approved the Ethiopian Statistical Service Proclamation unanimously on 30 June 2026](<https://www.fanamc.com/english/ethiopian-lawmakers-approve-carbon-market-tax-administration-statistical-service-proclamations/>), after [the Council of Ministers took up the draft on 26 May 2026](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_8922874>). No source found says the new proclamation has been published in the gazette. No decree, regulation or order made under either law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Gabon's statistics law is law 15/2014, amended by law 16/2022 of 6 September 2022. [Decree 0314/PR/MPP of 1 August 2024 approves the statutes of the National Institute of Statistics](<https://journal-officiel.ga/21242-0314-pr-mpp-/>) and cites the amended law as its basis. In the last twelve months, on 22 May 2026, [the planning minister presented to the Council of Ministers a bill amending ten articles of the law](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-conseil-des-ministres-vers-la-revision-du-cadre-legal-du-systeme-statistique-national/>). The bill would bring the law into line with the Constitution of December 2024. No source found shows the statistics council meeting under the law.

Ghana's statistics law is the [Statistical Service Act, 2019 (Act 1003)](<https://ghalii.org/akn/gh/act/2019/1003>), assented to on 24 September 2019. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, [the Service held a stakeholder engagement on a proposed Statistics Ghana Bill, 2026](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ghana-statistical-service_ghana-statistics-statsbill26-activity-7487065310030630913-ZlEw>). On 17 November 2026 [the Government Statistician said the draft bill would go to Cabinet and then Parliament](<https://www.myjoyonline.com/make-data-funding-compulsory-in-all-ministries-government-statistician/>). No decree, regulation or order made under the 2019 Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Guinea's statistics law is [Law L/2014/019/AN of 8 July 2014](<https://www.stat-guinee.org/images/Documents/Publications/Textes/loiStatistique2016.pdf>), which repealed the law of 1995. The statistics institute's compendium carries [the decree of 5 August 2015 on the national statistics council](<https://www.stat-guinee.org/images/Documents/Publications/Textes/loiStatistique2016.pdf>), and an order naming its members with the Prime Minister as president. All of it dates from 2015. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need the law applied in the past three years: its council or board appointed or meeting, a standard, release calendar or survey approval issued under it, a rule made under it, or a penalty.

The Gambia's statistics law is the [Statistics Act, 2005](<https://www.gbosdata.org/downloads-file/167-statistics-act-2005>). The bureau's strategy of September 2023 says [the Act is under revision and plans a review of the 2019 Statistics Bill](<https://www.gbosdata.org/downloads-file/526-national-strategy-for-the-development-of-stati>). In the last twelve months, in November 2026, [the bureau's Deputy Statistician-General called the 2005 Act outdated and asked for a revised law next year](<https://alkambatimes.com/gambias-20-year-old-statistics-law-cant-handle-ai-and-data-revolution-gbos-warns/>). No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Guinea-Bissau's statistics law is [Lei n.º 6/2007 of 10 September 2007](<https://stat-guinebissau.com/Menu_principal/Pubica%C3%A7%C3%B5es/Regulamento%20e%20Estatuto%20Organico/Legisla%C3%A7%C3%A3o_INE.pdf>), which sets up the national statistical system with its higher statistics council and institute. The institute's compilation also carries [Decreto n.º 4/2023 of 31 March 2023, the regulation of the law](<https://stat-guinebissau.com/Menu_principal/Pubica%C3%A7%C3%B5es/Regulamento%20e%20Estatuto%20Organico/Legisla%C3%A7%C3%A3o_INE.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need a council or board appointed or meeting, or a standard, rule or penalty under the law, in the past three years.

The national statistics strategy for 2022 to 2026 says [Law 3/2020 of 16 October 2020 governs statistical activity in Equatorial Guinea](<https://inege.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/ENDE-2022-2026-1.pdf>), replacing Law 3/2001 of 17 May 2001. [An African Union peer review in September 2025 credited the country with a modernised statistics law](<https://statafric.au.int/en/news/press-releases/2025-11-17/peer-review-progress-and-priority-actions-equatorial-guineas-nss>). It called for key decrees to be updated to align with it. On 10 December 2024 [133 trained statisticians were appointed to the statistics units of ministries](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/entrega_de_nombramientos_a_los_tecnicos_de_estadisticas_de_los_departamentos_ministeriales>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the 2020 law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Kenya's statistics law is the [Statistics Act (Cap. 112), assented to on 23 August 2006 and commenced on 1 February 2007](<https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/act/2006/4>), which establishes the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics. In the last twelve months, in April 2026, [the Bureau and the National Treasury published the Statistics Bill, 2026](<https://www.knbs.or.ke/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/The-Statistics-Bill-2026.pdf>). It would replace the Bureau with a Kenya Statistics Authority and repeal the Act. On 12 October 2026 [the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Budget reviewed the draft bill with Bureau officials](<https://peopledaily.digital/news/senators-push-bill-to-transform-knbs-into-kenya-statistics-authority>). The Act lists only two orders for a population census as subsidiary legislation. No other decree, regulation or order made under it has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Liberia's statistics law is the [National Statistics and Geo-Information Act, approved on 22 July 2004](<https://lisgis.gov.lr/document/lisgisact.pdf>), which sets up the statistics institute as an autonomous agency. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: [the institute's open data licence of June 2026](<https://liberia.opendataforafrica.org/atrwrfc>) is governed by the Act. The institute's entry for [the 2024 agricultural survey](<https://microdata.lisgislr.org/index.php/catalog/43>) says the Act guarantees respondents' confidentiality. No regulation made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Libya's statistics law is [Law No. 16 of 1963 on statistics and censuses, issued by King Idris I on 19 September 1963](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%d9%82%d8%a7%d9%86%d9%88%d9%86-%d8%b1%d9%82%d9%85-16-%d9%84%d8%b3%d9%86%d8%a9-1963-%d9%85-%d9%81%d9%8a-%d8%b4%d8%a3%d9%86-%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%a5%d8%ad%d8%b5%d8%a7%d8%a1%d8%a7%d8%aa-%d9%88%d8%a7%d9%84/>), which the Law Society's database lists as in force. In August 2024 the Libya Observer reported that a government meeting [addressed a committee's findings on reviewing and updating the 1963 law](<https://libyaobserver.ly/news/gnu-prepares-national-population-census>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Lesotho's statistics law is the [Bureau of Statistics Act, No. 8 of 2001](<http://www.bos.gov.ls/BOS_Act_2001.htm>). The African Union's peer review says [the Act established the Bureau, the national statistical system and the National Statistical Council](<https://statafric.au.int/sites/default/files/2025-12/ef_peerreview_lesotho_vf.pdf>), and needs modernising. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, [the Bureau's director told a media workshop that the Statistics Bill is expected to be enacted before the end of 2026](<https://sundayexpress.co.ls/?p=36134>). The reviewers had been told in August 2025 that a fourth Statistics Bill was being drafted. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Morocco's statistics text in force is [Royal Decree-Law no. 370-67 of 5 August 1968 on statistical studies](<https://unstats.un.org/unsd/dnss/docViewer.aspx?docID=46>). In the last twelve months, [Law 046.26 on official statistics was promulgated by dahir of 28 July 2026 and published in the Bulletin officiel of 10 August 2026](<https://canal212.ma/hcp-statistiques-gouvernance-reforme-maroc/>). [The Council of Government approved the bill on 2 July 2026](<https://www.linformation.ma/news/politique/le-conseil-de-gouvernement-approuve-un-projet-de-loi-relatif-au-systeme-statistique-national/64631>), and [the Chamber of Councillors adopted it unanimously on 13 July 2026](<https://lematin.ma/nation/le-parlement-adopte-la-reforme-du-hcp-et-des-statistiques-nationales/355927>). It takes effect only at the first meeting of the deliberative organ of the national statistics council. No source found dates that meeting, or names a decree, regulation or order made under either law. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Madagascar's statistics law is [Loi n° 2018-004 of 18 April 2018](<https://instat.mg/documents/upload/main/INSTAT_LoiStatistique2018-004_18-04-2018.pdf>), adopted by the Senate on 2 March 2018 and the National Assembly on 12 March 2018. The statistics institute [names the law as an institutional result achieved](<https://www.instat.mg/p/strategie-nationale-de-developpement-de-la-statistique-snds-deuxieme-generation-2023>) on its page for the 2023 to 2030 statistics strategy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Mali's statistics law is [Loi n°2016-005 of 24 February 2016](<https://sgg-mali.ml/JO/2016/mali-jo-2016-12.pdf>), published in the Official Gazette of 18 March 2016. The master plan says [the implementing decrees were taken in 2016](<https://instat-mali.org/laravel-filemanager/files/shares/ca/sdsmli20-24_ca.pdf>), and that the order appointing the National Statistics Council was taken only in 2018. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. [A methods manual of December 2025 cites its first article as the ground of statistical quality](<https://www.instat-mali.org/storage/319/manuel-harmonise-methodologie-collecte-statistique_pub.pdf>). No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need a council or board appointed or meeting, or a standard, rule or penalty, in the past three years.

Mozambique's statistics law is [Lei n.º 7/96 of 5 July 1996](<https://ieda.gov.mz/poema/EST-S1/EST-S1-Lei_7_96_de_5_de_Julho.pdf>), by which the Assembly of the Republic created the National Statistical System. The text held is an excerpt of the opening chapters, which set up the system and its bodies. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found, and no bill to amend or replace it. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Mauritania's statistics law is law no. 2005-017 of 27 January 2005. The national statistics strategy for 2021 to 2030 [lists it as the main text governing public statistical activity, and says it had not been revised](<https://afristat.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/17_SNDDS-2021-2030-plan-dactions-2021-2025.pdf>). The strategy records [decree no. 2006-024 of 17 April 2006 on the National Statistical Council](<https://afristat.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/17_SNDDS-2021-2030-plan-dactions-2021-2025.pdf>) and an order of 30 March 2008 appointing its members. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates an act done under the law since 2008. Mature would need a council or board appointed or meeting, or a standard, rule or penalty under the law, in the past three years.

Mauritius's statistics law is the [Statistics Act (Act 38 of 2000), which commenced on 2 April 2001](<https://statsmauritius.govmu.org/Documents/About_Us/Legislations/Statistics_Act_2000_All_Amended_Yr11.pdf>) and makes Statistics Mauritius the central statistical authority. The IMF's data review of September 2025 says [most recommended amendments were made through the Finance Act 2025](<https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/cr/2025/english/1musea2025003-source-pdf.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [Act No. 14 of 2026, assented to on 12 August 2026, amended the Act again](<https://mauritiusassembly.govmu.org/mauritiusassembly/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Act1426.pdf>), adding public sector debt to the statistics it covers. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Malawi's statistics law is the [National Statistics Act (Chapter 27:01), which commenced on 19 July 2013](<https://malawilii.org/akn/mw/act/2013/6/eng@2014-12-31>). It establishes the National Statistical Office and the National Statistical System. The text held stops partway through, so no later section has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Namibia's statistics law is the [Statistics Act, 2011 (Act No. 9 of 2011)](<https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2011/4777.pdf>), signed on 2 August 2011 and promulgated on 18 August 2011. The agency's [census release of October 2024](<https://nsa.org.na/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Media-Statement-2023-Census-Main-Report-30-October-2024.pdf>) says results are reported under the Act. [The national spatial data policy, signed on 24 February 2015, was developed under the Act](<https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2015/5684.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found since. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

Niger's statistics law is [Loi n° 2004-011 of 30 March 2004](<https://unstats.un.org/unsd/dnss/docViewer.aspx?docID=2129>), which creates the National Institute of Statistics and the national statistical system. In the last twelve months, [the Council of Ministers of 23 January 2026 adopted a draft ordonnance on the fundamental principles of statistical activities](<https://www.gouv.ne/index.php/les-communiques-du-gouvernement/1028-conclusions-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-vendredi-23-janvier-2026>). It would replace the 2004 law. No source found says the ordonnance has been signed, so the 2004 law stands. No decree, regulation or order made under that law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.
